'''Rebecca Killick''' is a British statistician whose work concerns [[Stationary process|non-stationary processes]] and [[Change detection|changepoint detection]]. They{{r|they}} are a professor of statistics at [[Lancaster University]],{{r|mathsci}} an affiliate of the centre for health informatics, computing, and statistics in the Lancaster University Medical School,{{r|chicas}} and co-editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of Statistical Software]]''.{{r|jss}}

==Education and career==
Killick completed a Ph.D. at Lancaster University in 2012, with the dissertation ''Novel methods for changepoint problems'' supervised by Idris Eckley.{{r|mg}}

After a year as a postdoctoral researcher, Killick returned to Lancaster University as a lecturer in mathematics and statistics in 2013, and added an affiliation with the centre for health informatics, computing, and statistics in 2021.{{r|chicas}} They were promoted to full professor in 2022.{{r|full}}

==Recognition==
Killick was named as 2019 Young Statistician of the Year by the European Network for Business and Industrial Statistics.{{r|enbis}} They were elected to the UK Young Academy in 2023, as part of its inaugural cohort of members.{{r|ukya}}
